How it's made

Pure ice cream, pressed like spaghetti

Every portion is 100% ice cream and made in front of you in under a minute — no scoops, no shortcuts. The press is the show.

1

The bed of cream

Freshly whipped cream goes into a chilled cup or cone first — it hides under the ice cream strands, just like the original in Germany.

2

The press

Vanilla gelato is pushed through a traditional Spaghetti Eis press, landing in long, perfect spaghetti strands.

3

Strawberry & white chocolate

A generous pour of strawberry sauce and a snowfall of white-chocolate shavings to finish. Sweet, creamy, unforgettable — Guten Appetit!

Our story

Mannheim, 1969 → Venice, today

1969

Invented in Mannheim, Germany

Dario Fontanella, the son of an Italian gelato maker, presses vanilla ice cream through a spätzle press in his father's Eiscafé in Mannheim — and Spaghetti Eis is born.

1970s→

Every German childhood

The sundae spreads to nearly every ice cream parlor in Germany. Today an estimated 25–30 million portions are served there every year — yet it stayed virtually unknown in the United States.

Today

Launching in Venice

Spaghetti Eis LA is founded by Lennart Heyner, a German immigrant who made Venice Beach his home. Our cart will source gelato, cream, and fruit from Los Angeles and California suppliers, serve in compostable packaging, and press every portion live in front of you.

2028

Ready for LA's biggest summer

We're preparing to serve at community and Games-time events around the 2028 Olympic & Paralympic Games — so visitors from every country can discover the dessert millions of Europeans grew up with.

Find the cart

A pop-up, based in Venice

No fixed shop — that's the plan. We're launching as a mobile pop-up: you'll find the cart at markets, festivals, street fairs, and private events across LA's Westside. Book us for your date, and we roll to you.

Good questions

FAQ

What is Spaghetti Eis?

It's pure ice cream: vanilla gelato pressed into spaghetti shapes, served on whipped cream with strawberry sauce and white-chocolate shavings. The sweetest spaghetti experience — creamy, fruity, and made to crave again and again.

Who invented Spaghetti Eis?

Dario Fontanella, son of an Italian gelato maker, in Mannheim, Germany, in 1969. He reportedly first tried a Mont Blanc dessert through a press, then applied the idea to vanilla gelato with strawberry sauce. It became a staple of German Eiscafés — and stayed a German secret for decades.

Do you have vegan or gluten-free options?

Yes. Any Spaghetti Eis can be made with plant-based vanilla gelato without whipped cream (vegan), and everything is available in a cup instead of a cone (gluten-free) — at no extra charge.

Where can I find the cart?

We're a new pop-up based in Venice Beach. You'll find us at markets, festivals, and private events across the Westside and greater LA — and the surest way to get your Spaghetti Eis is to book the cart for your own event above.

How far in advance should I book?

Two to four weeks is ideal for private events; festival and Games-time dates fill earlier. Short notice? Ask anyway — if the cart is free, we'll roll.
